introduction: The Animal Kingdom is broadly divided into Non-Chordates (without a notochord/backbone) and Chordates (with a notochord). At this foundational level, we will master the largest phyla of the invertebrate world and their defining characteristics, which are frequent one-liner questions.

core_concepts.title: Basis of Classification
core_concepts.description:
- **Symmetry:** Radial (body can be divided equally in any plane, e.g., Starfish, Hydra) vs. Bilateral (divided equally only in one plane, e.g., Humans, Insects).
- **Coelom (Body Cavity):** Acoelomates (no cavity, e.g., Flatworms), Pseudocoelomates (false cavity, e.g., Roundworms), and Coelomates (true cavity, e.g., Chordates).

core_concepts.title: Phylum Porifera & Cnidaria
core_concepts.description:
- **Porifera (Sponges):** Simplest multicellular animals. Possess a water transport/canal system. Their body is covered with pores (ostia). Example: Sycon, Spongilla.
- **Cnidaria / Coelenterata:** Possess stinging capsules called **Nematocysts** used for defense and capturing prey. Exhibit two body forms: Polyp (cylindrical, e.g., Hydra) and Medusa (umbrella-shaped, e.g., Jellyfish).

core_concepts.title: The Dominant Phyla (Arthropoda & Mollusca)
core_concepts.description:
- **Arthropoda:** The **largest phylum** in the animal kingdom (includes insects). Characterized by **jointed appendages** and an exoskeleton made of chitin. Examples: Mosquitoes, Crabs, Spiders, Butterflies.
- **Mollusca:** The **second-largest phylum**. Soft-bodied animals usually covered by a calcareous shell. Examples: Snail, Octopus, Squid, Pearl Oyster.

core_concepts.title: Worms and Annelids
core_concepts.description:
- **Platyhelminthes (Flatworms):** Dorso-ventrally flattened body. Mostly endoparasites. Example: Tapeworm, Liver fluke.
- **Annelida:** Body is segmented (metameres). Example: Earthworm (known as the farmer's friend), Leech.

important_entities.name: Echinodermata
important_entities.significance: All echinoderms are exclusively marine animals. They possess a unique **water vascular system** which helps in locomotion, capture of food, and respiration. Example: Starfish, Sea Urchin, Sea Cucumber.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Exam papers frequently test your ability to spot animals that have 'fish' in their name but are NOT true fishes (Pisces). 
- **Jellyfish** = Cnidarian.
- **Starfish** = Echinoderm.
- **Silverfish** = Insect (Arthropod).
- **Cuttlefish / Devilfish (Octopus)** = Mollusc.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever you see an insect or bug with jointed legs and a hard outer shell, instantly classify it as an Arthropod.

exam_strategy_tips: In SSC and Railway exams, identifying the 'Largest Phylum' (Arthropoda) and distinguishing 'False Fishes' are guaranteed questions. Memorize the exceptions clearly.
